headline: AI chip selloff returns as AMD sinks 8.8 percent and bitcoin breaks below 70,000 dollars
subhead: The S&P 500 fell 0.4 percent to 7,561.7 but gained 2.5 percent on the week, the 10-year yield rose to 5.15 percent after 6.5 percent annual PPI, and bitcoin fell 4.5 percent to 68,168.

us.text: S&P 500 fell 0.4 percent to 7,561.7 and the Nasdaq 0.9 percent to 25,136.3 as AMD dropped 8.8 percent and Broadcom 4.8 percent on profit-taking.
October PPI rose 0.3 percent for 6.5 percent annual wholesale inflation; the 10-year yield rose to 5.15 percent with a December Fed hike fully priced.
Week ahead: Nvidia reports Tuesday under interim CEO Colette Kress, and Anthropic is expected to price Wednesday at 70 to 78 dollars a share.

india.text: Nifty fell 155 points to 25,144.3 on 13 November, ending a three-day run, as October CPI rose to 6.09 percent and Brent neared 96 dollars.
FIIs net bought Rs 7,830.6 crore and DIIs net sold Rs 6,331.2 crore on 12 November, a ninth straight session of foreign buying.
Rupee fell 8 paise to 94.20 per dollar on 13 November on higher US Treasury yields and hawkish Fed comments.

global.text: Asia on 13 November: Nikkei closed at 61,142.35, while the Hang Seng fell to 23,637.60 and Kospi to 5,290.53 as chip worries lingered.
Europe: the FTSE 100 closed at a three-month high of 10,902.56 on insurers, energy and consumer stocks, while the DAX slipped.
Dollar index at a 52-week high of 103.4 and the euro at its lowest since April 2025 on bets of a larger Fed hike.

weekly.narrative: Jensen Huang's sudden exit as Nvidia CEO dominated the week: Nvidia fell 12.8 percent, but rotation into Apple, AMD and Broadcom still left the S&P 500 up 2.5 percent and the Nasdaq up 2.3 percent despite a Friday AI selloff. Hot US CPI and 6.5 percent annual PPI pushed the 10-year yield to 5.15 percent and left a December Fed hike fully priced, lifting the dollar to a 19-month high. That weighed on metals and crypto: gold fell 4.6 percent to a 13-month low, silver 6.1 percent and bitcoin 10.0 percent to below 70,000 dollars. India leaned on nine straight sessions of foreign buying and a bank rally, though the Nifty slipped to 25,144.3 on Friday after October CPI rose to 6.09 percent. Next week brings Nvidia results on 17 November, FOMC minutes on 18 November and Anthropic's expected Nasdaq debut on 19 November.
